extracted.intended_audience: writers, editors, copyeditors, and publishers (including self-published authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, and publishing books, journals, and other publications according to The Chicago Manual of Style (17th ed.). Covers manuscript preparation, typography, citation, and production practices for print and electronic formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions and parts of a book
rubrics_metrics.description: Books are traditionally organized into three major divisions: the front matter (prelims), the text (narrative), and the back matter (end matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front matter presents title/publisher/copyright and navigation; text contains arguments, data, illustrations, divided into chapters and sections; back matter contains sources, appendixes, indexes. A conventional outline and ordering of common elements is provided; few books contain all elements. Page counting: all pages (even blind folios) count in sequence. (See also recommended order of front/back items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-matter elements and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific front-matter items (half title, series title/frontispiece, title page, copyright page, dedication, epigraph, table of contents, lists of illustrations/tables, foreword, preface, acknowledgments, introduction, abbreviations, chronology) and their usual placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lowercase roman numerals for front matter pagination; display pages (half-title, title, copyright, dedication, epigraph) traditionally carry no folio; running heads omitted on display pages. Provide appropriate elements (e.g., title page with full title, subtitle, author/editor, edition, publisher/location). Self-publishers may omit publisher imprint or adapt arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering and pagination conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed books: recto (right) pages are odd-numbered, versos even-numbered; front matter uses lowercase roman numerals; text and back matter use arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count every page in the pagination sequence, even if folio is not shown. Drop folios (folio at bottom) and blind folios are discussed. Multivolume pagination may be consecutive across volumes or reset per volume; if consecutive, include volume in references. Reflowable electronic formats may lack fixed page numbers—use location information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads (headers) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads are top-of-page headings serving as navigational signposts; placement and content depend on book structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never use running heads on display pages or first page of table of contents/preface. Common arrangements include combinations of part title, chapter title, chapter number, subhead. For subheads used as running heads, use the last subhead on a recto page and the first on a verso. Omit running heads on part titles and chapter openings; include them where readers need orientation. Running feet (bottom) permissible in some books; electronic formats may use metadata or other navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title-page content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page should include full title, subtitle (if any), author/editor/translator name, edition number (if new edition), and publisher name and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No colon required between title and subtitle if typographically differentiated. Author name should be in preferred form (degrees/affiliations usually omitted). Publisher logo may appear. Self-publishers should publish under their own imprint or adapt accordingly; date should correspond to copyright date where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright page components
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical copyright page includes publisher address, copyright notice and dates, publication date/history, country of printing, impression line, ISBNs (each format), ISSNs (for serials), DOI (if any), translation/original-language info, acknowledgments and permissions, CIP data, paper durability statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at minimum a copyright statement and ISBNs for self-published authors. Copyright notice normally: © year name; may be followed by 'All rights reserved' and publication history. For continuously published resources include ISSN(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a new edition vs impression
rubrics_metrics.description: A new edition involves substantial changes to essential elements (text, notes, appendixes, illustrations), generally about 20% new/revised material; an impression is a reprinting with only minor corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate edition number (Second Edition, etc.) on title page; describe 'revised and expanded' when appropriate in prefatory material. Edition can also designate format or imprint differences (paperback, deluxe, electronic). Record edition information on the copyright page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impression number and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Impression (printing) lines and version numbers to indicate number and year of current printing and other versioning information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use impression line to show printing number and year; for version control across electronic and print workflows, maintain consistent version numbers and archival/versioning practices. See guidance on version numbers for multi-impression or multi-format works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation guidelines for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing manuscripts for submission, including formatting, pagination, front-matter requirements, and electronic-file considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow publisher-specific submission instructions; include required front matter, supply complete metadata, abstract, keywords. Electronic workflows are standard—provide files in requested formats, ensure consistent styles, supply high-quality image files and captions, and follow guidelines for tables and illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript editing best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and principles for manuscript editing covering substantive editing, copyediting, and preparing text for production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should preserve authorial voice while ensuring clarity, accuracy, and consistency. Use tracked changes or other collaboration tools, follow house style, check citations and permissions, and coordinate with production for typesetting and proofs. See sections on examples of editorial interventions and ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for proofreading copyedited and typeset manuscripts to catch remaining errors and verify technical and typographic correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofreaders should check pagination, running heads, folios, page sequence, consistency of headings, captions, tables, indexes, and bibliographic citations. Verify figure/table placement and legibility. Use standard proof-correction marks and follow a checklist for common errors (e.g., bad hyphenation, widows/orphans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and tables rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing, numbering, captioning, and placing illustrations and tables in books and journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear captions and credits; number figures/tables sequentially; place running heads and page numbers appropriately (may omit on pages with only illustrations). Supply high-resolution files, indicate preferred placement, and include illustration credits in back matter if not in captions. Use lists of illustrations/tables in front matter as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata, abstracts, and keywords for discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and publishers play roles in making works discoverable via metadata, abstracts, and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate metadata fields (title, author names, affiliations, abstracts, keywords), use keyword-search-friendly paragraph titles and headings, and supply abstracts and keyword sets per publisher guidelines. New coverage for metadata and keyword selection is emphasized to aid online discoverability and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for electronic formats and workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publishers have electronic workflows from manuscript to publication; electronic formats affect pagination, navigation, and version control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide metadata for electronic versions; consider reflowable vs fixed layout for e-books; include location markers where page numbers don't apply; keep permanent copies of cited online sources; be mindful of differences in appearance and navigation between print and electronic editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights, permissions, and copyright administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for securing rights, licensing permissions, and managing copyright issues for published works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand copyright law and licensing; include permissions and acknowledgments on copyright page; use publishing agreements and document subsidiary rights. Authors should secure permissions for third-party materials and track rights transfers; publishers must manage permissions processing and credit lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and source documentation (Notes and Bibliography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats and principles for notes and bibliographies covering basic formats, examples, and variations for many source types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present full bibliographic information in notes and bibliographies per Chicago's Notes & Bibliography system; follow specific rules for author names, titles, editions, publishers, and page ranges. Provide guidance and many examples for books, periodicals, websites, archival materials, multimedia, legal documents, standards, and more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-date reference system
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for the author-date citation style: in-text parenthetical citations with a reference list, including special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parenthetical citations with author, year, and page where appropriate; present a reference list with full bibliographic entries. Includes rules for formatting, special cases (multiple authors, corporate authors), and differences from Notes & Bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations for electronic and online materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed coverage for identifying and citing sources consulted online, including choice of link form, when to list time stamps, and when to keep permanent copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer DOIs when available; when citing websites/blogs/social media, include access dates where useful; include timestamps for time-sensitive posts; archive or save copies of sources when content may change; follow Chicago's examples for citing social media posts, comments, private messages, apps, video games, and other online formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DOIs and persistent identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preferring DOIs and other persistent identifiers for citing online materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite DOIs in stable form; when DOIs are absent, use stable URLs and consider archiving. Advice on when to include access dates and when to preserve a permanent copy is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing principles and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Components and general principles of creating indexes for books, including alphabetizing, punctuation, and typographical considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index compilers should identify components (headings, subentries, locators), follow consistent alphabetization rules (including treatment of word-by-word vs letter-by-letter), decide on inclusion/exclusion of variants, and punctuate indexes per Chicago guidance. Guidance covers editing an index compiled by someone else and typographic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and usage standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive guidance on grammar, syntax, word usage, parts of speech, and sentence structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prescriptions and descriptive guidance on sentence structure, syntax, use of singular 'they' and gender-neutral language, verb tenses, voice (active/passive), pronoun usage, and problematic word/phrase lists. Provides examples, common myths, and accepted alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation rules (commas, semicolons, colons, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance on punctuation use in relation to surrounding text—periods, commas, semicolons, colons, question/exclamation marks, hyphens, dashes, parentheses, brackets, slashes, quotation marks, apostrophes, spacing, and multiple punctuation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes chapter-length treatment of comma usage (including commas with phrases and clauses in all positions), punctuation with quotations, hyphenation vs en/em dash uses, spaces and nonbreaking spaces, and rules for lists and outline style. Examples and clarifications are provided for editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for when to hyphenate compounds, treatment of prefixes/suffixes, and word-division at line breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic rules for compound terms and hyphenation, guidance on compounds formed from proper names, and typographic considerations for hyphenation. Advice on nonbreaking spaces and division of slashes/dashes at line ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics, capitalization, and quotation-mark usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using italics, capitals, and quotation marks for emphasis, foreign words, titles, and special terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when to italicize non-English words, titles of works, and technical terms; when to use quotation marks; capitalization rules for names and titles; and consistency principles across a manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers: numerals vs words and number formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of when to spell out numbers versus using numerals, punctuation and plurals of numbers, inclusive numbers, and Roman numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules for ranges, ages, percentages, ordinals, and special numeric contexts (tables, equations). Discusses plurals and punctuation around numerals and recommendations for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and their treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on abbreviating names, titles, geographic terms, time designations, scholarly abbreviations, biblical abbreviations, and technology/science abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principles for introducing abbreviations, when to use periods, and lists of common abbreviations by category. Advice on maintaining readability and avoiding overuse of obscure abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages other than English: general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for handling non-English words, transliteration, diacritics, and language-specific conventions for Latin-alphabet and non-Latin scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance for languages using Latin alphabet, languages usually transliterated (classical Greek, Old English, etc.), American Sign Language, orthography requests (e.g., Hawaiian), and special typographic considerations. Advises on transliteration systems, diacritics, and when to italicize foreign-language terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations and dialogue handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for permissible changes to quotations, quotations' relation to surrounding text, quotation marks, ellipses, interpolations, and attributing quotations in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how to integrate quoted material, permissible editorial changes for clarity, punctuation and capitalization within quotations, use of ellipses and interpolations, and how to handle dialogue, drama, interviews, and field notes. Includes examples and attribution formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists, outline style, and vertical lists formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for list punctuation and format, vertical (block) lists vs run-in lists, and outline styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for punctuation of list items, capitalization, parallel structure, use of vertical lists as alternatives to tables, and the typographic treatment of nested lists. Practical manuscript prep advice and examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics in type and scientific notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for presenting mathematical expressions and preparing mathematics for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers style of mathematical expressions, inline vs display math considerations, symbol use, and preparation/editing of math in paper manuscripts; coordination with production for equations and figure quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of personal and organizational names, titles, and epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on styling personal names, titles and offices, epithets, kinship names, personifications, ethnic and socioeconomic group names, and names of organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for capitalization, ordering, honorifics, presentation of names in running heads and bylines, and cultural/linguistic considerations (e.g., Korean name presentation). Advises on consistency, respect, and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of digital-born content and multimedia citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for citing multimedia content (audiovisual recordings, video games, apps), and how to treat digital-born materials in citations and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples for citing clips/files, numbering, source citations for video and audio, and how to handle multimedia in notes and bibliographies. Advises on file formats, preservation, and linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing legal and public documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive coverage of citations for legal and public documents, updated to reflect The Bluebook and public-document conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes formats for bills, resolutions, congressional debates, hearings, reports, statutes, cases, and other public records. Advises on abbreviations, session and term numbering, and special treatments for historical documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for self-published authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of self-published authors' needs, including metadata, copyright, and procedures used by traditional publishers that can benefit them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-publishers are encouraged to follow traditional procedures: include title/copyright pages, ISBNs, provide metadata and keywords, consider open-access and distribution options, and attend to permissions and rights as a publisher would.
